Selected work

Design Excellence Award · SS 2025
Featured · Carolina Theatre Addition · SS 2025

Velare

Prof. David Thaddeus · Partner: Danielle Heckler

A contemporary addition to Uptown Charlotte's historic Carolina Theatre (1927). The building's wave-like massing echoes a curtain in motion — drawing from the mechanics of a theater valence and traveler to inform both façade and form. Glass surfaces drape at balcony recesses while a white exterior functions as a traveler, selectively opening to reveal interior moments. 15 floors activate the first seven with public programs including a restaurant, coffee shops, art gallery, and auditorium.

Transit Hub · FW 2024

Wave Station

Prof. David Thaddeus

A proposal for Charlotte's long-anticipated Gateway Station. A transitional threshold bridging residential, educational, and retail zones with the dense metropolitan core. Flowing geometry guides movement across the site while a public park offers civic pause — exposed steel supports carry a wave-like roof that frames views to the Charlotte skyline.

Catasta

Prof. Mark Manac · Partners: L. Hernandez, K. Truong, O. Ata

Design-Build · FW 2025

Paramorphic

Prof. Rachel Dickey · Partners: K. Truong, A. Chaaraoui, C. Ly-Hang

A design-build project exploring parametric form as a tool for an interactive chemistry pop-up environment for children. The design evolved through material selection, construction experimentation, and parabolic curve studies using tensioned string systems. Four key intents — sit, demo, display, shade — were individually prototyped then integrated into a single cohesive built form. Completed with an informative architectural animation documenting the full process.

Case Study · FW 2025

Water Cherry House

Architect: Kengo Kuma · Prof. Chris Jarret

A rigorous spatial study of Kengo Kuma's Water Cherry House, undertaken in a Japanese Spaces & Concepts course. The project began with an exercise in spatial reconstruction — locating and understanding the house using only publicly available images, without drawings or maps. This evolved into detailed diagramming, 3D modeling, plans, sections, axonometric drawings, and a 3D-printed model. Renderings were self-initiated to further explore the project's material and spatial nuances.
